function.mechanism: Forms viscous/gel hydrocolloid networks in water-rich systems, improving texture and physical stability.

adi.basis: EFSA (2018) retained the existing group ADI as temporary pending additional data and uncertainty resolution.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA found no carcinogenicity/genotoxicity concern for food-grade carrageenan in reviewed data, but kept ADI temporary and noted modeled high-percentile exposure exceedances in some groups.

adi.basis: JECFA record lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for carrageenan.

concerns.summary: Recent animal and human-cell studies report pro-inflammatory signaling and immune/oxidative changes in gut-related models after carrageenan exposure, though findings are not uniformly linked to barrier permeability changes.

A 2024 randomized double-blind crossover trial reported subgroup signals for reduced insulin sensitivity and higher inflammatory markers in overweight participants, despite no significant overall primary effect in the full cohort.

EFSA highlighted unresolved uncertainty around low molecular-weight carrageenan fractions and representativeness of test materials, supporting a temporary ADI rather than a finalized long-term guidance value.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018 did not identify carcinogenicity or genotoxicity concern for food-grade carrageenan in reviewed evidence.
JECFA lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for carrageenan.
A 2023 short-term pilot RCT in quiescent ulcerative colitis did not show significant worsening of primary clinical inflammation outcomes versus placebo.

populations: High-consuming toddlers in refined brand-loyal scenarios
High-percentile consumers across population groups in EFSA modeling
Infants in specific FSMP/special formula scenario modeling
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA (2018) reported refined brand-loyal exposure up to 758.6 mg/kg bw/day (toddlers) and stated high-percentile exposures could exceed the temporary ADI by up to about 10-fold in some scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Carrageenan remains approved in major jurisdictions, but EFSA retained only a temporary ADI and identified potential high-percentile exposure exceedances alongside unresolved uncertainties and emerging mechanistic/clinical concern signals in susceptible contexts.
key_factors: EFSA temporary ADI (75 mg/kg bw/day) with unresolved data gaps
Modeled high-percentile exposure exceedance up to about 10-fold in EFSA scenarios
Mixed but credible recent inflammatory/metabolic concern signals
IARC Group 3 classification for native carrageenan (distinct from degraded carrageenan Group 2B)
